requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: A LUKS2 volume was created, opened as /dev/mapper/secure, formatted with XFS, and mounted read-write at /srv/secure. The same LUKS UUID, active mapping, and mount were directly observed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: crypttab and fstab contain the automatic activation configuration. A bounded reboot changed the boot ID, after which the system was running, both crypt and mount units were active, /srv/secure was mounted, and the pre-reboot data checksum was recovered unchanged.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Direct pre- and post-reboot observations demonstrate an encrypted LUKS2/XFS volume at /srv/secure, automatic boot unlocking and mounting, preserved data, and a healthy node. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: The final evidence did not independently inventory /etc/fstab.pre-secure, so its continued presence is inferred from its creation and the absence of any later cleanup command.

operational_hygiene.summary: The mutations were narrowly connected to installing encryption support, creating and configuring the volume, testing activation, reboot verification, and final permissions. Package health remained good, no failed services or new listening sockets appeared, and temporary-file differences were ordinary reboot-generated systemd directories. One minor unnecessary residue was introduced: /etc/fstab.pre-secure was created as a rollback backup but no cleanup command removed it, so it is presumed retained. The attempted /etc/crypttab.pre-secure copy likely created nothing because crypttab was initially absent.
